summary: Elevated TTFB for chat completions after runtime/model upgrade impacting interactive sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for interactive chat completion requests immediately after a scheduled runtime and model catalog upgrade on 2026-03-11. Impact: degraded UX for live chat widgets (long initial spinner) and an increased rate of client-side timeouts on streaming endpoints.
Environment: Production (us-east), customer is on enterprise Dedicated plan (reserved capacity) with custom routing to dedicated pool.
Observed behavior: median TTFB increased from ~120ms to ~850ms for initial tokens; subsequent tokens show normal per-token latency once streaming starts. Error rate also shows increased 504s for client-side timeouts when clients abort before first token arrives.
Impact: Broad - affects ~25% of customer sessions during peak. Customer reports this has caused support tickets and a partial feature rollback request.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer-specific API key bound to dedicated pool (Acme Health).
2) Open chat completion session with system + user messages ~80 tokens total as prompt prefix.
3) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled and stream-first-token timeout set to 2 seconds on client side.
4) Observe initial spinner duration and measure TTFB via server timings header or telemetry dashboard.
logs: 2026-03-12T08:32:14Z [serving-runtime] session=abc123 ctx=init kernel_select: selected kernel ‘matmul_v3_fused’ latency=360ms
comments: 2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Carlos): Opened after customer report, included initial telemetry screenshots and a short gif from the customer showing long initial wait. Added as P1 due to enterprise SLA impact.

2026-03-12 10:20 - SRE (Maya): Confirmed TTFB delta in system dashboards for dedicated pool; spike aligns with runtime deployment v1.5.0 on 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC. Kicking off deeper investigation; tagging runtime and kernel teams.

2026-03-12 13:57 - Infra Eng (Liu Wei): Noted recent kernel-selector change in PR #2894 that prefers fused matmul kernels for certain shapes; hypothesis: increased synchronization cost for short sequences causing cold first-token penalty.

2026-03-13 08:40 - Customer (Acme Health - Jenna B.): We see the problem across both our web and mobile clients. Rolling back client timeouts is not ideal. Can you provide expected ETA for fix or a mitigation?

2026-03-14 11:12 - Support (Maya): Applied short-term mitigation: pinned customer routing to runtime v1.4.3 (pre-upgrade) for Acme dedicated pool and performed warm restart of model instances to repopulate KV caches. Customer reported immediate improvement to TTFB ~140ms. Preparing follow-up patch to runtime kernel selector.
2026-03-14 12:45 - Eng Lead (Priya Rao): Prioritizing revert of kernel-selector change in runtime v1.5.1 and adding a canary test for short-sequence TTFB before next rollout.
investigation_notes: Telemetry correlation: TTFB spike begins at 2026-03-11T23:40 UTC coincident with rollout of runtime v1.5.0 and updated model variants in catalog.
Profiling trace (sample): first-token spend concentrated in kernel selection and device sync points; wall-clock shows long host-side preparation (300-500ms) before enqueueing the first op to GPU.
KV-cache artifacts: in some containers ‘kv_cache_enabled’ flag was unset after model rollout which forced a fallback path that rebuilds prefix KV leading to extra CPU work on first request.
Autoscaler and capacity: no GPU shortages observed; dedicated pool maintained steady node count. Not a scaling capacity issue.

Related change: PR #2894 changes kernel preference ordering; appears to pick fused matmul for small batch/sequence scenarios causing non-optimal launch patterns on certain driver versions (NVIDIA 520.x).
Customer-specific routing: Acme was routed to a dedicated pool that was included in the v1.5.0 rollout due to an overlooked allowlist; this should have been excluded until canary passes.
Reproduction: reproduced in staging by applying v1.5.0 to a reduced-dataset workload and measuring first-byte latency; observed same 5-8x increase for initial token.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: pinned Acme Health to runtime v1.4.3 and performed controlled warm restarts of model instances to repopulate KV caches; customer confirmed restoration of expected TTFB (~120-160ms median). Long-term fix: revert kernel-selector ordering in runtime and add a short-sequence TTFB regression test to the canary suite. Patch PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2905 created and queued for expedited review. Post-deploy actions: run targeted canary for 48h in us-east with telemetry watch and add an allowlist check to prevent dedicated pools from being auto-included in early runtime rollouts.
next_steps: 1) Merge revert PR and deploy runtime v1.5.1 canary to subset of control plane on 2026-03-15.
2) Add short-sequence TTFB synthetic checks to pre-rollout CI and canary dashboards.
3) Update release checklist to exclude dedicated customer pools unless explicitly opted-in.
4) Follow up with Acme CSM and send postmortem notes and timeline; offer SLA credit if root cause confirmed as rollout mistake.
